author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: It was a matter of considerable doubt whether the fragile infant would draw breath enough to claim a name in this miserable world. Had he expired then, his biography would have possessed the rare and inestimable virtue of being incredibly brief, and entirely true.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: The wretched little creature gasped and struggled for that troublesome commodity, air. Providence, in its infinite mercy, had spared him the presence of profound medical men and weeping aunts; leaving him solely to the tender mercies of a pauper nurse, steeped in gin, and Nature herself.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: With a sudden, sharp cry that pierced the gloom of the parish ward, the infant announced his arrival; a sound which fluttered the tattered blankets of a nearby bed, where a pale and exhausted young woman lay dying.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: She pressed her cold, white lips to the infant’s forehead in a final, desperate kiss of maternal love, shuddered violently, and fell back into the eternal sleep. The parish surgeon, accustomed to such trifling parish matters, looked on with profound indifference.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: “It’s all over, Mrs. Thingummy!” declared the medical gentleman, casually adjusting his spectacles as he gazed upon the lifeless clay.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: “Ah, poor dear, so it is!” echoed the misty-eyed nurse, her attentions far less fixed upon the departed soul than upon the green glass bottle she had hastily concealed.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: “If the troublesome little brat cries, give it some gruel,” instructed the surgeon, drawing on his gloves. “A remarkably good-looking girl, that. One wonders what gutter she crawled out of.”

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: “The overseer brought her in last night,” croaked the old woman. “Found her dying in the street, she was. Her shoes were worn to dust, but from whence she came, only God Almighty knows.”

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: Lifting the cold left hand, the surgeon shook his head with a cynical smile. “The old story,” he muttered. “No wedding-ring. A familiar tragedy! Good night!”

author: Charles Dickens
ai_styled_text: Thus the medical gentleman departed to his warm dinner; whilst the nurse, fortifying herself with another robust draft from the green bottle, sat by the dying fire to clothe the parish orphan.
